page_title: BBC Learning English - English at Work / The plastic aubergine
title: The plastic aubergine
topic: Language to use in an 'elevator pitch'
description:
Anna's about to pitch her plastic vegetable idea to Paul, but will she have the chance to speak to him? The only opportunity may be very short – Anna will need to get her elevator pitch perfect if she's going to be successful!
This episode focuses on what to say when you have limited time to pitch a new idea, perhaps in a lift or elevator.
phrases: We've come up with an exciting new product.
This fantastic product will be a great addition to table decorations in the cafe and restaurant market.
We can increase efficiency but maintain quality.
By my calculations, we can increase profits by 20%.
I'm confident this new product will be a huge success.

listening_challenge.question: How much does Anna hope her new product will increase profits by?

transcript.speaker: Narrator
transcript.text: Hello and welcome to English at Work. The company's computer system has been fixed and Anna seems to have found a new friend in Dave, the IT support man. But her main concern now is pitching her new idea for a plastic aubergine, to Paul the boss.

transcript.speaker: Tom
transcript.text: So Anna, that guy didn't really know what he was doing did he?

transcript.speaker: Anna
transcript.text: You mean Dave?

transcript.speaker: Tom
transcript.text: Dave – was that his name? He had a really bad smell.

transcript.speaker: Anna
transcript.text: No he didn't. He's done a great job. Look everything is working so, if you don't mind, I think we should get this pitch for Paul finished.

transcript.speaker: Denise
transcript.text: You'd better hurry up. Paul's taking the afternoon off to go to his biscuit lovers’ convention.

transcript.speaker: Tom
transcript.text: Oh right. Well, we might as well leave it until tomorrow then Anna.

transcript.speaker: Anna
transcript.text: No Tom. There’s no time like the present – I heard someone say that once – we've got to get our idea to Paul as soon as possible. Then we might have time for a drink, or shall I ask Dave?!

transcript.speaker: Tom
transcript.text: No, no, you're right. Look, I'll design some pictures of the aubergine and you get the results of our survey together, yeah?

transcript.speaker: Anna
transcript.text: Great.

transcript.speaker: Narrator
transcript.text: Well done Anna. Remember to make your pitch clear and exciting. Really sell it with words like 'exceptional!', 'fantastic!', 'quality', 'profit', 'efficiency', and 'value for money'.

transcript.speaker: Anna
transcript.text: OK, I've got all that. I'm just adding some of the facts and figures from our customer survey.

transcript.speaker: Tom
transcript.text: Anna, I've got the designs, they're coming off the printer now.

transcript.speaker: Paul
transcript.text: Denise, I’m off now. Can’t wait any longer for my garibaldis!

transcript.speaker: Anna
transcript.text: Wait Paul! I need to tell you about our new product idea.

transcript.speaker: Paul
transcript.text: Well, I, I, have to go. Can you tell me about it in the lift?

transcript.speaker: Anna
transcript.text: In the lift? Do I have to?

transcript.speaker: Paul
transcript.text: Sorry Anna, but that's the only time I’ve got.

transcript.speaker: Narrator
transcript.text: Right Anna. It's time for your 'elevator pitch' – an elevator is an American word for lift. You’ll need to pitch your idea quickly and concisely. You need to tell Paul what the product is and who your market is. Then talk about how you hope it will make money for the company. Talk about the evidence you have that it will be successful and convince him it will really benefit the business.

transcript.speaker: Anna
transcript.text: Phew, there's a lot to say in a short time but here goes.

transcript.speaker: Paul
transcript.text: Anna, could you just press the 0 button there, thanks.

transcript.speaker: Anna
transcript.text: Now Paul. Tom and I have come up with a new exciting product – the plastic aubergine.

transcript.speaker: Paul
transcript.text: Oh yes?

transcript.speaker: Anna
transcript.text: Yes. This fantastic product will be a great addition to table decorations in the café and restaurant market.

transcript.speaker: Paul
transcript.text: Will it now? Do you really think it will be a profitable addition to our plastic portfolio?

transcript.speaker: Anna
transcript.text: Oh yes. Using the same plastics as our fruits, we can easily re-mould our bananas and change the colour. We can increase efficiency but maintain quality.

transcript.speaker: Paul
transcript.text: And profits?

transcript.speaker: Anna
transcript.text: By my calculations, we can increase profits by 20%. That's based on selling the same quantity that we now sell of Imperial Lemons.

transcript.speaker: Paul
transcript.text: Hmm, 20%, really? But do you know who’s going to buy this product?

transcript.speaker: Anna
transcript.text: I do. We've conducted a survey and already found 10 new companies who would buy this and 27 existing customers who have shown an interest in it…

transcript.speaker: Anna
transcript.text: …and I'm confident this new product will be a huge success.

transcript.speaker: Paul
transcript.text: Very impressive. You've certainly done your homework. Look, let me chew it over – probably on a custard cream – and I'll get back to you.

transcript.speaker: Anna
transcript.text: Thanks. Paul, Paul… you've forgotten your bag.

transcript.speaker: Paul
transcript.text: Oh yes, I'll need that. Thanks.

transcript.speaker: Narrator
transcript.text: Great work Anna! You convinced me but have you convinced Paul?
So Anna's done her first 'elevator pitch' and kept to the facts. Here's a reminder of some of the things she said:
We've come up with an exciting new product.
This fantastic product will be a great addition to table decorations in the café and restaurant market.
We can increase efficiency but maintain quality.
By my calculations, we can increase profits by 20%.
I'm confident this new product will be a huge success.

transcript.speaker: Tom
transcript.text: So, how did it go Anna?

transcript.speaker: Anna
transcript.text: I'm not sure. I told Paul as much as I could and I think he listened.

transcript.speaker: Tom
transcript.text: Good, good. So, what are you doing now?

transcript.speaker: Anna
transcript.text: I've got to meet someone.

transcript.speaker: Tom
transcript.text: Anyone I know?

transcript.speaker: Anna
transcript.text: No, not really.

transcript.speaker: Tom
transcript.text: It's Dave from IT isn't it? What does she see in him?

transcript.speaker: Narrator
transcript.text: Do you want me to answer that Tom?! Anna may have fallen for the charms of Dave but let's hope she keeps her mind on her plastic aubergines. Join us again next time on English at Work.
